INSTRUMENT CORRECTION, NOT AN ARTIFACT REGRESSION. score_hold_justification: The overall rises 6.8 to 7.0, exactly the measured noise floor, and that understates the round. Two of the eleven categories moved on instrument correction rather than on anything the implementer did: applying the rubric's new hard mappings costs accessibility 1.5 and payload 0.5, or 0.18 off the eleven-category mean, for an artifact whose measured accessibility and payload are unchanged. Scored on the anchor's own unmapped numbers for those two rows the overall would be 7.1. Against that, the genuine artifact deltas are strongly positive and broad: chrome restraint +2.5 and colour discipline +1.0 are the two largest single-category moves this loop has recorded, and they discharge the anchor's I2 (impact 8) and most of I3 and I6. They are held from compounding by one severe regression and by the untouched per-template backlog. Information density and list-and-table craft are held rather than raised for a reason that matters more than the arithmetic: S1 and S2 improved how a row READS without changing how much a screen DELIVERS. /wiki lost 61px of 3624 and /catalog 398px of 13427, under 3% each, while /wiki now leaves 55% of the shell empty across all 85 rows and /data about 44%. The anchor's complaint was 950px of dead space INSIDE the row; the fix moved that dead space OUTSIDE the row. The invariant R7 states is satisfied and the reading experience is genuinely better, but the residue is unspent, which is the contract's relocated-defect case and is filed as I16. List craft holds at 5.5 because its large gain (I4 resolved: name-to-attribute distance cut from ~950px to ~40px on two templates) is offset by a new alignment defect on /wiki (I17), by I1 and I11 being untouched, and above all by I15, which leaves the site's primary table with column labels lying on top of its first two data rows in both themes at both viewports.

items.problem: The /catalog column-header row is displaced downward and lies on top of its own first data rows, at scroll position zero, in both themes and at both viewports. Measured rects at 1440x900: thead occupies y 462-491 while tbody row 1 occupies 445-477 and row 2 occupies 477-508, so the header intersects two body rows. At 390x844: thead 905-934 against rows 868-899 and 899-930. The displacement equals --header-h exactly (46px at 1440, 129px at 390, matching .site-header's measured offsetHeight). The captures show the consequence plainly: MODEL / PROVIDER / IN / OUT / CONTEXT / STATUS / READ are printed over 'Anthropic Claude Haiku Latest' and 'Anthropic Claude Sonnet Latest', and at 390 the word MODEL appears stranded between the third and fourth rows of the list. This is a regression introduced by S7 against a baseline that rendered the header correctly. It is not a capture artifact: it reproduces in a live browser via getBoundingClientRect at both viewports, and the baseline captures at the same settings show no displacement. The site's primary surface, a 396-row price table, currently has no legible column labels. Note also that S7's premise was false: .table-wrap declares overflow-x: auto, and per CSS overflow the visible cross-axis coerces to auto, so .table-wrap computes overflow-y: auto and IS the thead's nearest scrolling ancestor. The thead therefore never stuck to the viewport and .site-header could never have occluded it. The iteration-0 item I7 asserted that collision from CSS alone and was wrong.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/table-catalog--light--1440.png, table-catalog--dark--1440.png, table-catalog--light--390.png (all three against their baseline/ counterparts, which show the header correctly placed); live getBoundingClientRect over out/catalog.html at 1440x900 and 390x844
items.invariant: At scroll position 0 on /catalog, at 1440 and at 390, the table's column-header row shall not intersect the bounding box of any tbody row; and once /catalog is scrolled, the column headers shall remain visible and unoccluded.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R11 — checked, and R11 itself is implicated. R11 was written from iteration-0 I7 and assumes .site-header and the thead share one scroll context. They do not, while .table-wrap is a scroll container. R11 should be amended to a two-sided condition: the column headers shall be neither occluded by the site header NOR displaced onto the rows they label. R2 must stay satisfied, so .table-wrap keeping overflow-x: auto is not negotiable; any remedy that removes the horizontal container scroll to fix this trades an R11 defect for an R2 defect.
items.prescription: Hypothesis, not a specification — the last one here was wrong, so re-derive from the rendered geometry before editing. The cheapest correct move is probably to revert .data-table thead th to top: 0, since inside the .table-wrap scroll container that yields zero displacement and the site-header collision the offset was defending against cannot occur there. If genuine viewport-sticky column headers are wanted on a 13,000px table, the container itself has to stop being the scroll context for the thead, which is a larger change than this defect warrants. Whatever is chosen, verify by reading both rects at scroll 0 AND after a scroll, not by reading the --header-h token.

items.prescription: Declare two tracks and use only those: a reading track at --measure and a full track at --shell. Then either narrow --shell on the row-index templates so the rows are not stranded in a container twice their width, or fill the residue with content the page already owns. Do not widen --measure-list back out; the row itself is now correct.

items.problem: New defect introduced by S1. .browse-row is grid-template-columns: minmax(0, var(--measure-list)) auto auto, and each row is its own independent grid, so the two auto tracks size to that row's own content and nothing aligns across rows. The kind column starts at a constant x~538 because the first track is fixed, but the status column starts wherever that row's kind word happens to end: ACTIVE begins at roughly x=578 after 'org', 584 after 'tool', 585 after 'event', 592 after 'model', 603 after 'concept' and 620 after 'technique'. Down 85 rows the status column is a ragged left edge with six distinct positions, so the one thing a reader scans this index for vertically — which records are dead — cannot be scanned vertically. The anchor had no alignment defect here; the columns were merely too far apart. Stripe's mechanism is the direct contrast: it treats a listing as one table so every column shares one track across all rows, which is what makes a status column scannable at a glance.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/index-wiki--light--1440.png and its mid-list region (rows DeepSeek through Moonshot AI), current/index-wiki--dark--1440.png
items.invariant: In a row-based list surface, every column shall begin at the same x position on every row of that surface.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R7 — checked and binding. R7 requires the label column bounded to --measure-list and the remedy keeps it; the change is only to the two trailing tracks. R8 is unaffected, since no rule is added.
items.prescription: Give the list a shared track set rather than per-row auto tracks — either promote the container to a grid with grid-template-columns: var(--measure-list) 8rem auto and let rows be display: contents, or fix the kind track to a width that fits the longest kind word ('technique'). Either makes the status column a single vertical edge.

items.target: evidence rig (tools/ui-evidence.mjs capture procedure and tools/ui-invariants.mjs id S7)
items.problem: Re-filed and widened, because this round demonstrated the gap rather than predicting it. Two parts. First, all 40 captures remain full-page renders at scroll position zero, so no state that exists only after scrolling is judgeable, on a site with a 13,029px table and two sticky elements. Second and more serious: the registered DOM invariant S7 asserts only that the table head's top is not above the site header's bottom after a 400px scroll. That is a ONE-SIDED condition. Pushing the thead arbitrarily far DOWN — including onto the rows it labels, which is what shipped — satisfies it trivially. The manifest reports 5 registered, 5 pass, and the gate was read as evidence the change was safe, while the artifact was in fact broken at every scroll position including zero. An invariant that can be satisfied by making the artifact worse in the opposite direction is the same failure class as R5's preserved post-mortem: a check that passes for the wrong reason.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json (40 entries, every one a full-page top-of-document capture); tools/ui-invariants.mjs lines 200-224, whose check returns true whenever thTop >= headerBottom - 0.5 and tests nothing else; contrast with the measured overlap in I15
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R11 — the rule this invariant claims to enforce, and which it under-enforces.
items.prescription: Do not change the artifact for this item. Make the S7 check two-sided: assert both that the thead is not occluded by the site header AND that its rect does not intersect any tbody row rect, at scroll 0 and after a scroll. Separately, add one viewport-sized capture per long route taken after scrolling about 1200px, labelled distinctly (table-catalog--light--1440--scrolled.png), so sticky behaviour becomes a judgeable evidence class. Add to JUDGE.md's Known evidence lies: 'L3 — a full-page capture does not show the scrolled configuration of sticky elements' and 'L4 — a one-sided geometric invariant can be satisfied by displacing the element in the opposite direction; assert both bounds.'

What remains is that the column renders the identical string '2026-08-31' on all 396 rows and so discriminates nothing while consuming a seventh of the table's width, and that it is the direct cause of the route's tab burden: /catalog still reports 817 focusable elements, which is 396 model links plus 396 date links plus controls. A keyboard reader passes two stops per row where one would do, and that duplication is what exhausts the focus sweep in I12 — which now costs the artifact 1.5 scored points via the accessibility mapping.

Removing the column removes no information from the page — the same date is already stated once in the header line 'last checked 2026-08-31' — so slot 1's content prohibition is not engaged. Where a row's read date genuinely differs, show it on that row only — the same exception-only principle R8 now applies to badges. Reclaim the freed width for the price columns, which also helps I1.

items.problem: Unchanged from the anchor and slightly more exposed now that the feed's row rules are gone. The home page's right rail stops at roughly y=630 while the changed-feed beside it continues to y=2691, leaving about 2000px of empty column down the middle of the site's front door in both themes. The rail carries the property's highest-value orientation content — the 396-model count, the deprecated-and-retired list, the latest post and latest tutorial — and occupies well under half the height available to it. The feed's own rows still have ragged heights because the trailing 'source' link wraps to a second line on roughly half of them, so the two-column band reads as neither a settled grid nor a continuous list.
items.invariant: The home page's secondary rail shall not terminate more than one feed-row height above the end of the primary feed column beside it, and a feed row's trailing source link shall occupy its own track rather than wrapping.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R6 — checked and binding: R6 requires changed-feed lines visible above the fold at 1440x900 and 390x844, currently passing at 12 and 4. Any rebalancing must keep both counts non-zero. This is a RESTRUCTURE and subject to KP1.
items.prescription: Either extend the rail with content already on the page — the 'EVERYTHING HERE' section below the feed is the obvious candidate, and moving it into the rail fills the void and shortens the page without adding or changing copy — or end the two-column band where the rail ends and let the feed run full width below it. Separately, give the feed row a fixed grid so 'source' occupies a right-aligned track instead of wrapping.

items.problem: Unchanged from the anchor. Every /tools listing renders the same four fields for all 35 entries — licence, pricing model, verification date and link — as a single run-on mono line separated by middots, wrapping to two lines at the full width. The fields are identical in kind across every entry, which is the definition of tabular data, but they are set as 35 sentences of differing length. A reader comparing what each tool costs must read 35 prose runs instead of scanning one column. The site already demonstrates it can do this correctly: /catalog aligns the same class of data into columns, and /wiki and /data now do the same for two fields.
items.invariant: Where every entry in a listing carries the same set of fields, those fields shall be presented in aligned columns rather than as a delimited run of inline text.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R2 and R7 — checked: any columnar treatment must not introduce page-level horizontal scroll at 320px, and the mobile form must collapse to stacked label/value rather than repeating I1's failure of hiding columns behind a container scroll. R7's --measure-list is the natural bound for the name track. Whatever ships must also satisfy I17's cross-row alignment condition.
items.prescription: Give .listing a shared grid of name / licence / pricing / verified tracks bounded well inside the shell, aligning the four fields down the page within each category section. Below 33.999rem, stack them as label/value pairs. This is a presentation change only: the same strings appear, in the same order, under the same headings.

items.problem: Unchanged from the anchor. There is no @font-face, no next/font and no bundled face anywhere in app/. Type is a fallback chain — Charter, Bitstream Charter, Sitka Text, Cambria, Georgia, Times New Roman — plus a system mono stack. The serif/mono split is a genuinely good domain choice, serif for argument and mono for every dated machine-read fact, and it is applied with discipline. The defect is the chain: Charter, Sitka Text, Cambria, Georgia and Times New Roman differ materially in x-height and set width, so the same page resolves to a different face on macOS, Windows and Linux. The controlled 38rem measure therefore yields a different character count per platform and the rhythm built on --step--1 through --step-4 lands on different baselines, which means the typographic system this verdict credits is only actually true on machines that happen to have Charter installed. Vercel's mechanism is the direct contrast: one face chosen for the property and served with it, so the grid's rhythm is identical for every reader.
items.evidence: app/globals.css lines 55-57 and the absence of any @font-face across app/; rendering visible in loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/article--light--1440.png and prose--light--1440.png
items.invariant: The resolved body face shall be identical across platforms — either self-hosted, or a stack whose fallbacks are metric-compatible with the primary via size-adjust.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R3 — checked and binding: first-load payload must stay under 150 KB gzipped, worst route currently 122.2 KB, leaving about 28 KB of headroom. R3 as written measures JavaScript, so a woff2 face would not count against it as specified; say so explicitly rather than assuming, and prefer a subset under 30 KB either way.
items.prescription: Self-host one subset woff2 for the serif (Charter is openly licensed) with font-display: swap and a size-adjust-tuned local fallback, so the measure and rhythm resolve identically everywhere. If R3 is read to cover total payload rather than JS alone, subset to Latin plus the figures actually used.

items.problem: Re-filed at raised impact, because the rubric's new accessibility mapping now reads this ratio directly and it costs the artifact 1.5 scored points. The sweep on /catalog reports 'PASS — 150 of 817 focusable element(s) — STOPPED AT THE 150-STOP CAP, the rest unswept'. It records a PASS having examined 18% of the route, and the 667 unexamined stops are precisely the deep-table region most likely to differ from the swept header region. This is the failure mode R5's own preserved post-mortem exists to prevent, reappearing as a cap instead of an early return. R5 requires a traversal to assert its stop count against the page's actual focusable count; the check does compute and print both, they disagree by 667, and it still records PASS. The artifact may well be fine; the oracle cannot say so, and it is claiming that it can. The other three routes sweep their complete tab order and would map to 10.
items.evidence: scripts/verify-design.mjs output, focus indicators section: '/catalog — 150 of 817 focusable element(s) — STOPPED AT THE 150-STOP CAP, the rest unswept'; contrast '/tools — the complete tab order, 98 stop(s)'
items.prescription: Do not change the artifact for this item. Make the sweep record FAIL, or a distinct INCOMPLETE outcome that does not count as a pass, whenever swept is less than focusable. If the 150-stop cap exists for runtime reasons, replace exhaustive sweeping with a sample that always includes the last stop and a random interior stop, and report the sampling explicitly. Note that I8, if accepted, cuts /catalog from 817 stops to roughly 421 and makes a full sweep cheap enough to simply do.

items.target: app/wiki entry page template and app/colophon (section headings inside a measure-bounded block)
items.problem: S5 bounded .facts to --measure but the FACTS section heading's own rule still spans the full shell. On /wiki/concept/ai-winter the FACTS label sits at x=145 with a rule running to x=1295 while the definition list beneath it stops at x=751 — the rule is 2.1 times the width of the block it introduces. The same page gets it right twice immediately below, where the REFERENCED HERE and APPEARS IN rules stop at their own columns' edges, so the correct idiom is present on the same screen as the incorrect one. This is exactly the condition R10 was written for, on the page R10 came from.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/wiki-entry--light--1440.png (FACTS rule to x=1295, facts block to x=751, REFERENCED HERE rule correctly to x=435)
items.invariant: A horizontal rule introducing a content block shall not exceed that block's own rendered width.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R10 — checked and directly binding; this item is R10 not yet being true for section headings inside the entry template. The enforcing invariant for R10 evidently checks the blocks S5 named and not their headings.
items.prescription: Apply the same max-width: var(--measure) bound to the section heading element that introduces .facts, or move the rule onto the .facts block itself. Widen the R10 invariant to assert heading rules as well as block rules.

items.problem: Unchanged from the anchor and still unresolvable by this loop. /catalog presents 396 rows as one continuous table with four filter controls and no pagination or grouping beyond an A-to-Z sort within provider. Whether a reader who arrives knowing only 'I want a cheap long-context model' can converge on one is a question about that reader's behaviour, not about the pixels: the filters may be entirely sufficient, or the row count may defeat them. No screenshot answers it, and the axe, reflow, payload and traversal oracles are all silent on it. Listed so it stops resurfacing as an actionable layout finding — the density and column work in I1 and I8 should not be justified by findability claims this loop cannot test.
items.prescription: Keeper decision. Resolving it needs a real reader attempting a real lookup, which is outside this loop's oracle stack. If the keeper wants it closed, the cheapest instrument is a timed task with three people, not another screenshot.
